speaker: interviewer
text: Hello Grace, thank you for joining. Can you see and hear me alright?

speaker: interviewee
text: Yes, perfectly. My daughter showed me how to use this video thing last Christmas, so I'm an expert now.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha, wonderful. So this is just about your grocery orders, there are no wrong answers.

speaker: interviewee
text: Good. Thirty-five years of teaching and I still don't like being tested.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Great. Tell me a bit about your household and who does the food shopping.

speaker: interviewee
text: It's just me now. I taught primary school for thirty-five years and I retired four years ago. I do my own shopping, and I like to cook properly, even for one.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. And how did you hear about Shmuber Eats?

speaker: interviewee
text: My daughter. She lives two hours away and she worries. She said, Mum, try it for a couple of months, see if you like it better than the bus. So I'm trying it.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Walk me through your last Shmuber Eats order, from opening the app to putting things away.

speaker: interviewee
text: I made my list, I typed it in very slowly, and it came the next day. I'd planned a baked salmon with lemon and dill for Sunday. But instead of a salmon fillet they sent a packet of smoked salmon slices, the kind for sandwiches, and you can't bake those, they'd just turn to leather.

speaker: interviewer
text: Smoked slices for a baked fillet? What did you end up making?

speaker: interviewee
text: Scrambled eggs with smoked salmon. Very nice, but not what I'd planned, and I'd bought the dill specially.

speaker: interviewer
text: Do you think the picker saw them as the same thing?

speaker: interviewee
text: I think the picker saw the word salmon. A fishmonger would have laughed.

speaker: interviewer
text: That's really helpful, thank you. Was anything else difficult with the order?

speaker: interviewee
text: Oh, yes, one thing. When I got to the very end, to pay, it threw me out, it logged me out completely, and I had to ring my daughter to remember my password.

speaker: interviewer
text: Okay. Great. Let's move on. How often do you order groceries online?

speaker: interviewee
text: About once every two weeks, since the spring. My daughter checks I'm still doing it.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Tell me about the last time an item in your order was substituted.

speaker: interviewee
text: Apart from the salmon? The bread, quite often. They send a different loaf. That I don't mind, bread is bread.

speaker: interviewer
text: And do you get a message before they swap?

speaker: interviewee
text: Sometimes my phone buzzes, but by the time I've found my glasses, it's already decided.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Great. How do you keep track of what you need between orders?

speaker: interviewee
text: A notebook by the kettle. My daughter wants me to use the list in the app, but I like the notebook.

speaker: interviewer
text: Would it help if your daughter could add to a list in the app too?

speaker: interviewee
text: Oh, she'd love that. She'd add vegetables. I'd delete them.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Great. How did you pick the delivery window last time?

speaker: interviewee
text: I chose the morning, nine to eleven. I'm always up early, and in the afternoon I have my choir on Wednesdays.

speaker: interviewer
text: And has it ever come outside that time?

speaker: interviewee
text: Once, it came at twelve. A bit late, but they sent a message.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. What would you think of a monthly delivery pass, and what would you pay for it?

speaker: interviewee
text: I'm on a pension, so I'd have to think. If it really saved money, perhaps five.

speaker: interviewer
text: And at 9.99 a month?

speaker: interviewee
text: No, that's too much for twice a month. I'd rather pay for each delivery.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. Would you recommend Shmuber Eats to a friend?

speaker: interviewee
text: To my friends from choir, maybe, the ones who don't drive anymore. Yes.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. What do you like most?

speaker: interviewee
text: Not standing at the bus stop with heavy bags in the rain.

speaker: interviewer
text: And what do you like least?

speaker: interviewee
text: The writing in the app is small, and there are too many pictures of things I didn't ask for.

speaker: interviewer
text: Noted. Great. Have you tried the recipes section?

speaker: interviewee
text: I have my own recipes, thank you.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha, fair. Great. On a scale of one to ten?

speaker: interviewee
text: Seven. Eight if the salmon had been salmon.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. And how did your daughter feel about it?

speaker: interviewee
text: She's pleased. She says I sound less tired on the phone on Mondays.

speaker: interviewer
text: That's lovely. Did you leave a review in the app?

speaker: interviewee
text: No. I wouldn't know where.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Last question, is there anything about your orders I didn't ask about?

speaker: interviewee
text: No, I think you were very thorough, dear.

speaker: interviewer
text: Thank you so much, Grace, this was really helpful.

speaker: interviewee
text: My pleasure. Goodbye.
